summary: Diagnosed the Jose V12 pinned-source failure in real Chromium and proved that the immutable V11 .html.gz.b64 source is itself corrupted: the HTTP 200 text contains a literal [...ELLIPSIZATION...] marker inside the base64 stream, clean length is not divisible by four, and window.atob correctly rejects it. The job definition explicitly forbids rewriting a corrupted V11 payload merely to make the wrapper pass, so no LAB candidate decoder change or source rewrite was made. The SHA gate remains fail-closed and product authority is unchanged.
tests: HTTP_RESPONSE_CAPTURE_PASS: Chromium observed status 200, type cors, content-type text/plain; charset=utf-8.
BASE64_SHAPE_FAIL_PROVEN: clean_length=19886, clean_length_mod_4=2, eight non-base64 characters found around clean index 9865.
CORRUPTION_MARKER_PROVEN: exact raw context contains literal [...ELLIPSIZATION...] between otherwise base64-looking spans.
ATOB_FAILURE_REPRODUCED: InvalidCharacterError reproduced deterministically in Chromium.
NO_FALSE_REPAIR_PASS: decoder was not changed to strip or ignore missing-data corruption.
SHA_GATE_PRESERVED_PASS: expected decompressed digest remains 0cf9a40fb53e977dccb40c9755d668a3ee922ccd61883f19229bb4a113139a05 and no bypass was added.
AUTHORITY_MUTATION_PASS: no Catalog, Current, Lineage, Human Accepted or Served pointer changed.
unresolved: Locate an existing byte-exact V11 source whose decompressed SHA-256 is 0cf9a40fb53e977dccb40c9755d668a3ee922ccd61883f19229bb4a113139a05; do not reconstruct missing bytes from the corrupted base64 artifact.
Publish a new integrity-checked material reference only if the exact bytes are found, then repoint the LAB candidate source without weakening its SHA gate.
Rerun real Chromium verification through SHA PASS, topic-local 12-level/3-round map checks and V12/V11 A/B toggle.

If no exact source exists, return a boundary with SOURCE_DEBT instead of fabricating a replacement.
